steps.title: Read what happened to the described entity
steps.body: A past passive participle describes an entity affected by an action. The supplied form сде́ланный has the meaning done/made. The form напи́санный means written, and уби́тый means killed. These words describe what was done to the entity; they do not identify it as the person doing the action. The three supplied meanings differ by the underlying action. Choosing written for сде́ланный would replace doing or making with writing; choosing killed would replace it with killing.

steps.title: Recognize the supplied long forms without inventing a universal algorithm
steps.body: The retained examples are long past passive forms with adjective-type endings. In the shown сде́ланный and напи́санный forms, the formation contains double n; уби́тый has t. The retained source shows these forms from perfective verbs. This lesson recognizes the supplied forms; these endings alone are not a complete productive formation rule for every verb. Broader formation includes other suffix patterns and lexical restrictions, so do not manufacture an unlisted form from this small set. An imperfective past passive can exist; the supplied perfective examples are not a universal claim that every past passive must come from a perfective verb.

steps.title: Distinguish the action meaning from long versus short form
steps.body: The meaning written belongs to напи́санный, not to the doing/making form сде́ланный or the killing form уби́тый. The meaning killed belongs to уби́тый, not to the other two actions. The retained short form напи́сан has a single n and lacks the long adjective ending shown in напи́санный. Long versus short form is different from the action meaning: both writing forms concern writing. These checks select the action meaning of a supplied form; they do not test production of all short-form gender and number endings.

steps.title: Identify the writer in the retained passive sentence
steps.body: письмо написано Иваном — the letter was written by Ivan. The letter is the entity affected by the writing; Ivan is the writer identified in the retained sentence. The passive form describes the letter’s state or result, rather than saying that the letter writes somebody. The short passive form in the sentence differs from the long headword напи́санный. A longer sentence supplies context that a headword lacks; do not infer a writer, reader or exact time from a bare participle alone. Active participles are outside this required Unit27 lesson.

sessions.title: Optional: distinguish a present passive form from its supporting verb forms

steps.title: Meaning differs between a passive description, a finite verb and an infinitive
steps.body: The supplied обсужда́емый has the meaning being discussed. It describes something affected by discussion, rather than naming the person doing the discussing. The source also permits an able-to-be-discussed reading; the checked English option here is being discussed. The supporting verb form оставля́ем means we leave: it is a first-person plural present-tense form, with we performing the action, not a passive description. The infinitive оставля́ть means to leave and does not by itself name a we subject. Choose we leave for the finite form and to leave for the infinitive. The option to discuss is an infinitive meaning rather than the checked passive description. Different action meanings and grammatical functions must not be exchanged simply because forms share a stem.

steps.title: Recognize only the retained formation and accent placements
steps.body: The retained source illustrates the relation between the infinitive оставля́ть, the finite form оставля́ем and the present passive оставля́емый with its adjective ending. The finite we leave form is a supporting example, not itself a participle. This small set does not establish which other verbs permit a present passive or a complete formation algorithm for every verb. In the supplied leave contrast, оставля́емый is retained and оставляемы́й is rejected. In the supplied discuss contrast, обсужда́емый is retained and обсуждаемы́й is rejected. The retained accents are on the third syllable; the alternatives move them to the final syllable. Compare the accented vowel in each particular form; do not predict an unlisted form or its stress from this set. This entire session is optional and non-gating. Its present-passive stress choices belong to the optional objective, not to the required past-passive stress gate. Active-participle instruction belongs to Unit 29, not this session.

sessions.title: Read the described letter, writer and separate main action

steps.title: Separate the letter description from the sentence action
steps.body: Письмо, написанное Анной, лежит на столе. means the letter Anna wrote is on the table. The participial phrase написанное Анной describes the letter: written is the action affecting it, and Anna is the named writer. The main statement locates the letter on the table. Being written and being on the table are separate parts of the reading. Neither the table nor the letter is the writer. The sentence does not say that Anna put the letter away, and the writer is not identified as its reader. A passive participle describes the affected entity; an agent phrase can name the person responsible for that particular action.

steps.title: Do not transfer the main-action subject to an unnamed participle agent
steps.body: Анна убрала прочитанное письмо. means Anna put away the letter that had been read. Anna performs the putting-away action; the description прочитанное письмо says that the letter had already been read. The sentence does not name the reader. Anna might or might not have read it; neither reading can be asserted from this sentence alone. Already read is different from just written or still reading aloud. The supplied passive description expresses the completed reading of the letter, not an ongoing action by Anna. Recognize the main verb, the affected letter and any explicitly named agent separately. These checks interpret the supplied readings; accent placement alone cannot answer who wrote or read the letter, and recognizing these examples does not demonstrate production of an unfamiliar participial sentence.

sessions.title: Locate stress in the two required past passive forms

steps.title: Place the accent on the supplied vowel
steps.body: The required past passive forms are напи́санный and прочи́танный. Each displayed accent is on the second syllable. For the guided write form, stem stress напи́санный is the supplied option; later-vowel stress написа́нный moves the accent to the vowel in the third syllable and is rejected for this supplied form. It is not an accent on the final adjective ending. For the independent write contrast, напи́санный is retained and написа́нный is rejected. For the read contrast, прочи́танный is retained and прочита́нный is rejected. Compare the accented vowel in the same letters rather than simply noticing that both options have an accent mark.

steps.title: Keep required past-passive stress separate from optional reference and general production
steps.body: The supplied limit is no stress rule is admitted beyond these four. The competing statement these four placements generate every other participle wrongly turns four retained reference placements into a productive rule for an unlisted participle. Two of the four belong to optional present-passive reference, while the required checks here use only the two displayed past-passive forms. Optional present-passive checks do not gate Unit27 advancement. The fact that these two past forms share second-syllable stress does not predict stress for every other participle or its short forms. Use verified lexical evidence for an unlisted form. Meaning recognition and accent placement are separate tasks.

| написа́ть ''(to write)'' – напи́са'''нн'''ый (written) / напи́са'''н''' (short form)
|}

{| class="wikitable"
| уби́ть ''(to kill)'' – уби́'''т'''ый (killed) / уби́'''т''' (short form)

Письмо, написанное Анной, лежит на столе. means the letter Anna wrote is on the table. The participial phrase написанное Анной describes the letter: written is the action affecting it, and Anna is the named writer. The main statement locates the letter on the table. Being written and being on the table are separate parts of the reading. Neither the table nor the letter is the writer. The sentence does not say that Anna put the letter away, and the writer is not identified as its reader. A passive participle describes the affected entity; an agent phrase can name the person responsible for that particular action.
Анна убрала прочитанное письмо. means Anna put away the letter that had been read. Anna performs the putting-away action; the description прочитанное письмо says that the letter had already been read. The sentence does not name the reader. Anna might or might not have read it; neither reading can be asserted from this sentence alone. Already read is different from just written or still reading aloud. The supplied passive description expresses the completed reading of the letter, not an ongoing action by Anna. Recognize the main verb, the affected letter and any explicitly named agent separately. These checks interpret the supplied readings; accent placement alone cannot answer who wrote or read the letter, and recognizing these examples does not demonstrate production of an unfamiliar participial sentence.
